title: Outputs bind snapshot renderers to typed plugin sinks

nodes.summary: Outputs bind KB renderers to configured sinks over one selected root
nodes.detail: An output binds a KB-authored renderer, which may compose dependent queries, to a configured sink connector whose input type it produces; every read uses the same selected root. Browsing never updates an external output, sink invocation needs no evolution, and changing an output definition or sink configuration is an ordinary evolution.

realised.evidence: PR #229: `root output publish` prepares one selected root, resolves the sink from that root's plugin configuration, renders the registered query and invokes the sink; browsing and preview never publish, and outputs/sink config live in accepted kb.dhall and plugin config

nodes.summary: One pure snapshot-read form for queries and renderers
nodes.detail: Queries and renderers are KB code, not function-valued facts, and share one registered form returning a SnapshotRead Program interpreted against the selected snapshot; pure calculations are lifted, and SnapshotRead permits no acquisition, sink invocation or publication.
sections: Decision / Root data and authored declarations

realised.evidence: PR #27 implements the shared SnapshotRead Program algebra for queries (renderers never built)

nodes.summary: Output GADT pairs renderer with a generated typed SinkBinding
nodes.detail: `Output` takes the renderer function and a generated `SinkBinding input` that cannot be forged from a source connector or mismatched sink; KbDefinition holds existential SomeQuery/SomeOutput lists from which generated registration supplies names, contracts and codecs.
sections: Decision / Root data and authored declarations

realised.evidence: SinkBinding/KbDefinition/SomeOutput never appeared in code (the 'Output' identifier at seq 6 is unrelated)

nodes.summary: Queries stay independently callable via queryRoot on a Validated root
nodes.detail: queryRoot runs a query by descriptor and checked arguments against a Validated Root, with RootExecution checking contracts, so Web/MCP can show structured results without a renderer or sink and without reimplementing calculations in JS.

realised.evidence: queryRoot code_added at seq 26 over structurally checked roots; the Validated Root gate arrives at seq 27 (PR #28)

nodes.summary: prepareOutput checks renderer result against the sink's input contract
nodes.detail: Preparation evaluates the renderer in RootExecution (no PluginInvocation) and checks its result against the sink binding resolved from the same root. PreparedOutput is an ordinary, unretained value; a later update may re-render and need not reproduce a preview.

nodes.summary: Large payloads use immutable ArtifactStore references
nodes.detail: Large file/document inputs may reference immutable artifacts (bytes plus media type) that must resolve to fixed bytes or fail; this is optional, not a universal document conversion, and no generic Destination type is added.

nodes.summary: Delivery capability explicitly invokes sinks and records outcomes
nodes.detail: A host Delivery effect (InvokeSink, InspectDelivery) lowers to PluginInvocation and filesystem plumbing, persists dispatch intent before acting and validates results. The first file sink is a first-party plugin whose relative paths resolve against the KB directory; normal updates use an accepted snapshot.

realised.evidence: No Delivery effect or sink plugin exists; PluginInvocation (seq 78) serves acquisition only

nodes.summary: Sink failures: idempotency per sink, Uncertain outcomes, no rollback
nodes.detail: Sinks declare idempotent replacement versus non-idempotent actions; pre-dispatch failures are distinct from Uncertain dispatch, which is never silently retried, and sink failure cannot roll back accepted knowledge or external effects.

realised.evidence: No delivery outcome types in code ('Acknowledged' at seq 92 is curation, unrelated)

nodes.summary: Generated per-KB Query alias; renderers are `args -> Query input`
nodes.detail: The query/renderer form becomes the SDK Query monad specialised by a generated `type Query a = SDK.Query Root a`; the root is implicit and queries compose directly in do-notation instead of threading an explicit root.
sections: Decision / Root data and authored declarations

realised.evidence: PR #27 generates the root-specific Query alias and collection bindings

nodes.summary: queryRoot returns QueryResult with an ordered read trace
nodes.detail: Query invocation returns the checked result together with the ordered snapshot-read trace from ADR 0009, laying ground for future query explanation without committing to a predicate language.

realised.evidence: QueryResult code_added at seq 26; PR #27 returns ordered traces

nodes.summary: Outputs registered in kb.dhall naming renderer export and sink reference
nodes.detail: Instead of an authored Output GADT and SinkBinding, outputs are kb.dhall entries naming a renderer export and a plugin/instance/method SinkReference. The host inspects both signatures and generates an adapter that type-checks renderer result against sink input; the manifest is the authority.
sections: Decision / Root data and authored declarations

realised.evidence: No output registration, OutputDefinition or SinkReference exists in code

nodes.summary: Outputs registered in kb.dhall naming a registered query and sink
nodes.detail: An output registration names a query from the same root's queries list and a plugin/instance/method SinkReference; renderer is the role of that query, not a second export. The host inspects the query and sink signatures and generates an adapter type-checking query result against sink input, rejecting unknown entries, mismatches and source connectors.
sections: Decision / Root data and authored declarations

realised.evidence: PR #229 adds OutputDefinition {name, description, query, sink}; OutputBindings compiles a generated KyynOutputBinding adapter checking the query result type against the sink input type, and rejects unknown queries, non-publish methods and source connectors

nodes.summary: Queries are public typed read interfaces; no contract versioning
nodes.detail: Consumers rely on a query's declared argument/result types rather than the KB's internal fact layout, so authors can keep the interface while changing storage schemas. Kyyn exposes the checked contract but adds no contract versioning or compatibility guarantees.
sections: Decision / Root data and authored declarations

realised.evidence: PR #228 adds `root query list/show/execute`; show renders each query's checked argument and result contracts without running it. No versioning machinery exists, as the decision requires

nodes.summary: Output preparation exposes argument, input, options and result contracts; preview never writes
nodes.detail: OutputDescriptor carries query-argument, sink-input, sink-options and result contracts plus the bound sink. Preview only prepares the value, never invokes a sink or creates directories, shows the configured sink and its checked configuration, and claims no resolved destination; it is optional, not an approval step.

realised.evidence: PR #229: `root output show` reports query input, content, options, defaults, result and configuration; `preview` renders the query as the sink's typed input and shows sink and configuration without dispatch. Built as a composition over queryRoot with PreparedOutput holding the binding, not a separate prepareOutput operation

nodes.summary: Query arguments and sink options are separately typed and checked
nodes.detail: Query arguments determine content; sink options control one invocation. Each has its own plugin/KB-authored type and checked value, options never mutate accepted sink configuration, the sink declares typed defaultOptions, and invalid options cause no invocation. The guest boundary is `publish :: Config -> Options -> Input -> Program SinkCalls (Either SinkError Result)`.
sections: Decision / Query arguments and sink options

realised.evidence: PR #229 adds SinkConnector registration with publish and defaultOptions exports and compiler-derived config/options/input/result contracts; publish decodes --options against the options contract (or uses the default) separately from query --input

nodes.summary: Delivery invokes the sink with checked options; no ledger or delivery ID
nodes.detail: Delivery's InvokeSink takes the prepared value and separately checked options and returns Acknowledged/FailedBeforeDispatch/RejectedByDestination/Uncertain without persisted dispatch intent, delivery IDs or InspectDelivery. Publishing is one action over one selected accepted root, with no CAS, approval handshake or persistent receipt; the first file sink remains a first-party plugin with KB-relative paths.

realised.evidence: PR #229 adds the Delivery effect (InvokeSink connector options input) returning PublicationOutcome, interpreted by running the guest sink and lowering FileWrite requests to FileSystem.publishBytes against the KB scope; no ledger or IDs. Lowers via GuestExecution/FileSystem rather than the PluginInvocation signature the ADR sketches

nodes.summary: local-file File sink atomically replaces a UTF-8 text file
nodes.detail: local-file adds a sink whose input is Text, configured with a path and an optional per-invocation pathOverride. It writes UTF-8, creates parents, replaces via temp file and atomic rename (no CAS, symlink replaced, umask permissions), resolves relative paths against the KB, and returns the absolute path or propagates SinkError.

realised.evidence: PR #229 adds LocalFile.Write (Config path, Options pathOverride, defaults, publish via writeTextFile) and publishBytes (createDirectoryIfMissing, temp file, renameFile); Delivery resolves paths against the KB scope and returns the absolute target

nodes.summary: SinkError maps to delivery outcomes; uncertainty without recorded outcomes
nodes.detail: A guest SinkRejected maps to RejectedByDestination and SinkUncertain to Uncertain; a Right result is Acknowledged only after its result contract checks; protocol loss, guest failure or invalid results after dispatch are Uncertain. Without records, a crash may leave no result and the destination is inspected before retrying. Idempotency remains sink-specific and nothing rolls back.
sections: Decision / Query arguments and sink options

realised.evidence: PR #229's Delivery interpreter maps Rejected/Uncertain sink errors, checks results against the result contract, and reports failures as Uncertain once a write was dispatched and FailedBeforeDispatch otherwise. Only the idempotent file sink exists, so there is no per-sink idempotency declaration yet

notes: The output half of this ADR went unbuilt for over 170 steps: until seq 179 the only realised parts were the query mechanics shared with 0008/0009 (seq 26). Seq 143 redesigned the unbuilt output declaration, replacing the authored Output GADT, SinkBinding and existential KbDefinition with kb.dhall named-entry registration. That was a spec-only rewrite of a spec-only design. Seq 177 (PR #226, design-only, Tom-approved) reshaped it again just before implementation. An output now names a registered query rather than a renderer export (0017.12 replaces .11). Query arguments and sink options became separately typed (.15), and the local-file text sink got a concrete contract (.17). The Delivery ledger, dispatch intent and delivery IDs were dropped, so .07 is replaced by .16 rather than refined, because its 'persist dispatch intent and record outcomes' guarantee was withdrawn. Preparation/preview (.14) and failure mapping (.18) are refinements. The 'queries are public typed read interfaces' paragraph became its own node (.13). Seq 180 (PR #229) built nearly all of it in one step, realising .01, .12 and .14-.18; seq 179 (PR #228, root query commands) realises .13. Calls a reviewer should check: preview and publish are compositions over queryRoot rather than a prepareOutput/PreparedOutput operation as sketched (.14 medium). Delivery lowers through GuestExecution and FileSystem rather than the PluginInvocation constraint the ADR shows (.16 medium). Only the idempotent file sink exists, so the per-sink idempotency distinction in .18 is untested. ArtifactStore (.06) is still unbuilt. The seq 26 'future directions' paragraph (SQL-like query explanation, host-side query execution) is explicitly disclaimed as not a commitment, so I left it out of the nodes. Founding and seq 177 Verification demands (Web/MCP queries, HTML preview isolation) produce no nodes.
